1:6.t: "Expanse" translates the KJV's "firmament": the vault of the sky that separates the waters above from the waters below.

1:21.t: "Great sea creatures": the KJV says "great whales"; the Hebrew word covers any large sea animal.

1:26.t: "Mankind": the KJV's "man" here means the human race, as verse 27 ("male and female") shows.
"Us", "Our": capitalized as God speaking of Himself.

"Mankind", "the man" (Hebrew adam): adam is both the word for a human being or humankind and, later, the name Adam. It sounds like adamah, "ground", so the man made from the ground (2:7) is named for it.

3:22.t: "Us", "Our": capitalized as God speaking of Himself.

2:7.t: "Mankind", "the man" (Hebrew adam): adam is both the word for a human being or humankind and, later, the name Adam. It sounds like adamah, "ground", so the man made from the ground (2:7) is named for it.

"Living being" (Hebrew nephesh): the KJV's "living soul". Nephesh means a living, breathing creature, a whole person, not a soul separate from the body. It is also used of animals (1:20, 1:24). Elsewhere it is translated soul, life, person or self, depending on the setting.

2:12.t: "Aromatic resin": the KJV's "bdellium", a fragrant gum.

2:13.t: Cush: the KJV says "Ethiopia", its usual rendering of the Hebrew Cush, a land south of Egypt.

2:14.t: Tigris: the KJV gives the Hebrew name, Hiddekel.

2:18.t: "A helper who is right for him": the KJV's "an help meet for him", where "meet" means suitable.

"Helper" (Hebrew ezer): this word does not mean an assistant of lower rank. In the Old Testament it is used most often of God Himself as the helper of His people (Psalm 121:1-2). "Right for him" (kenegdo) means "corresponding to him", a partner who matches him.

2:20.t: "A helper who is right for him": the KJV's "an help meet for him", where "meet" means suitable.

3:15.t: "He will bruise your head": the KJV says "it", meaning the woman's offspring. Christians have long read this verse as the first promise of Christ.

"Offspring" (Hebrew zera, "seed"): the word is a collective singular, so it can mean one descendant or many. The KJV's "seed" keeps this ambiguity, and Paul builds on it in Galatians 3:16. We use "offspring" or "descendants" depending on the setting.

4:1.t: "Was intimate with": the KJV's "knew", meaning sexual relations.

4:7.t: "His desire will be for you, and you will rule over him": as in the KJV. Many modern Bibles read this as sin's desire for Cain, which he must master.

4:21.t: "Lyre and flute": the KJV's "harp and organ"; the organ meant here is a simple pipe.

4:22.t: Bronze: the KJV's "brass", which in 1611 meant copper or bronze.

5:2.t: "Mankind": the KJV says "called their name Adam"; the Hebrew adam means mankind.

5:6.t: Enosh, Kenan, Mahalalel: the KJV spells these Enos, Cainan and Mahalaleel.

6:2.t: "Sons of God": the KJV wording is kept. Interpreters differ on whether these were angels or the line of Seth.

6:4.t: "Sons of God": the KJV wording is kept. Interpreters differ on whether these were angels or the line of Seth.

6:3.t: "My Spirit": capitalized as the Spirit of God.

6:6.t: "Regretted": the KJV's "it repented the LORD", meaning God was grieved and sorry, not that He had sinned.
"Regretted" (Hebrew nacham): the word means to be sorry, grieved or moved to change course. It describes God's real grief at human evil, not an admission of a mistake (compare Numbers 23:19).

6:9.t: "Blameless": the KJV's "perfect", meaning whole and upright.

6:16.t: KJV: "in a cubit shalt thou finish it above".

10:6.t: Put: the KJV spells it Phut.

10:11.t: "Asshur went out": as in the KJV. The Hebrew can also mean that Nimrod went out to Assyria, as many modern Bibles read it. Rehoboth-ir: the KJV's "the city Rehoboth".

10:24.t: Shelah: the KJV spells it Salah.

11:12.t: Shelah: the KJV spells it Salah.

11:7.t: "Us": capitalized as God speaking of Himself.

11:9.t: Babel sounds like the Hebrew word for "confuse".

12:6.t: "Plain of Moreh", "plain of Mamre": as in the KJV. The Hebrew word likely means a large tree, so many modern Bibles read "oak" or "terebinth".
Shechem and 12:8 Ai: the KJV spells them Sichem and Hai.

13:18.t: "Plain of Moreh", "plain of Mamre": as in the KJV. The Hebrew word likely means a large tree, so many modern Bibles read "oak" or "terebinth".

14:13.t: "Plain of Moreh", "plain of Mamre": as in the KJV. The Hebrew word likely means a large tree, so many modern Bibles read "oak" or "terebinth".

12:9.t: "The south": the Negev, the dry region in the south of Canaan.

13:1.t: "The south": the Negev, the dry region in the south of Canaan.

13:3.t: "The south": the Negev, the dry region in the south of Canaan.

14:1.t: "King of nations": the Hebrew is Goiim, which may be a place name.

14:9.t: "King of nations": the Hebrew is Goiim, which may be a place name.

14:10.t: "Tar pits": the KJV's "slimepits", pits of bitumen.

14:14.t: "Relative": the KJV's "brother", used here for Lot, Abram's nephew.

14:16.t: "Relative": the KJV's "brother", used here for Lot, Abram's nephew.

14:15.t: "North of Damascus": the KJV's "on the left hand of Damascus", facing east.

14:19.t: "Owner": the KJV's "possessor"; the Hebrew can also mean Creator.

14:22.t: "Owner": the KJV's "possessor"; the Hebrew can also mean Creator.

15:2.t: "Lord GOD": the KJV prints GOD in capitals where the Hebrew has God's personal name after "Lord".

15:17.t: "Smoking firepot and a flaming torch": the KJV's "smoking furnace, and a burning lamp".

16:13.t: "The God who sees me": the KJV's "Thou God seest me". Beer-lahai-roi means "well of the Living One who sees me". The second half of verse 13 is hard to read in Hebrew; the KJV's "Have I also here looked after him that seeth me?" is followed.

17:1.t: "Blameless": the KJV's "perfect", meaning whole and upright, as at 6:9.

"God Almighty" (Hebrew El Shaddai): the meaning of Shaddai is uncertain. The Greek and Latin translations took it as "the Almighty", and the KJV followed them. Others connect it with "mountain" or "the One who is sufficient".

17:5.t: Abram means "exalted father"; Abraham sounds like "father of many".

18:6.t: KJV: "three measures of fine meal" (three seahs).

18:10.t: "About this time next year": the KJV's "according to the time of life".

18:14.t: "About this time next year": the KJV's "according to the time of life".

18:19.t: "I have chosen him": the KJV's "I know him", meaning known in the sense of chosen.

19:5.t: "Have sex with them": the KJV's "that we may know them".

19:14.t: "Who were to marry": the KJV's "which married" can mean either already married or engaged.

20:16.t: "Pieces of silver": the KJV does not name the unit; if shekels, about 11.5 kilograms of silver. "To cover the offense": the KJV's "a covering of the eyes", a payment that clears her honor. "Cleared": the KJV's "reproved", in the old sense of set right.

21:9.t: "Mocking": the Hebrew word plays on Isaac's name and can also mean playing.

21:14.t: "Skin of water": the KJV's "bottle", a container made of animal skin.

21:31.t: Beersheba means "well of the oath" or "well of seven". The KJV spells it Beer-sheba.

21:33.t: "Grove": as in the KJV. The Hebrew names a tamarisk tree.

22:1.t: "Tested": the KJV's "tempt", in the old sense of put to the test.

22:14.t: Yahweh-yireh: the KJV's Jehovah-jireh, meaning "the LORD will provide" or "the LORD will see to it".

22:21.t: Uz: the KJV spells it Huz.

23:3.t: "Hittites": the KJV's "sons of Heth" and "children of Heth".

24:2.t: "Under my thigh": a solemn way of taking an oath.

24:9.t: "Under my thigh": a solemn way of taking an oath.

24:10.t: Mesopotamia: the Hebrew is Aram-naharaim, "Aram of the two rivers".

24:22.t: KJV: an earring of "half a shekel weight" and bracelets of "ten shekels weight of gold". "Nose ring": the KJV's "earring", which 24:47 places "upon her face".

25:15.t: Hadad: the KJV spells it Hadar here.

25:20.t: "Aramean": the KJV's "Syrian". Paddan-aram: the KJV spells it Padan-aram.

25:25.t: Esau sounds like the Hebrew for "hairy". 25:26 Jacob means "he grabs the heel", a phrase for one who deceives.

25:27.t: "Quiet": the KJV's "plain", meaning whole or settled.

26:8.t: "Caressing": the KJV's "sporting with", a play on Isaac's name.

26:20.t: Esek means "quarrel", Sitnah "hostility", Rehoboth "wide places" or "room".

26:33.t: Shibah: the KJV spells it Shebah. It means "oath" or "seven".

27:28.t: "Grain": the KJV's "corn", meaning grain of any kind.

27:37.t: "Grain": the KJV's "corn", meaning grain of any kind.

27:36.t: "Cheated": the KJV's "supplanted", a play on the name Jacob.

27:39.t: "The richness of the earth": as in the KJV. The Hebrew can also mean "away from the richness of the earth", as many modern Bibles read it.

28:12.t: "Ladder": the Hebrew may mean a stairway.

29:17.t: "Weak": the KJV's "tender eyed"; the Hebrew may mean soft or delicate.

29:32.t: Reuben means "see, a son" and sounds like "He has seen my misery"; Simeon sounds like "heard"; Levi sounds like "attached"; Judah sounds like "praise".

30:6.t: Dan means "judged"; Naphtali "my wrestling"; Gad "good fortune"; Asher "happy"; Issachar sounds like "reward"; Zebulun sounds like "honor"; Joseph means "may He add".

30:14.t: Mandrakes were plants thought to help a woman become pregnant.

30:37.t: "Almond, and plane trees": the KJV's "hazel and chesnut".

31:42.t: "The One whom Isaac feared": the KJV's "the fear of Isaac".

31:53.t: "The One whom Isaac feared": the KJV's "the fear of Isaac".

31:47.t: Jegar-sahadutha (Aramaic) and Galeed (Hebrew) both mean "heap of witness". Mizpah means "watchtower".

32:24.t: The man is not named. Jacob says he has seen God, and Hosea 12:4 calls him an angel, so pronouns for him are left lowercase.

32:28.t: "Israel": the name likely means "God strives" or "he strives with God". The explanation given in the verse plays on the verb sarah, "to struggle".

33:18.t: "Arrived safely at the city of Shechem": the KJV reads "came to Shalem, a city of Shechem". The Hebrew word can be a place name or mean "safely".

33:19.t: "Pieces of money": the Hebrew is kesitah, a unit of unknown value.

33:20.t: El-elohe-Israel means "God, the God of Israel".

35:7.t: El-bethel means "God of Bethel". 35:8 Allon-bacuth means "oak of weeping"; the KJV spells it Allon-bachuth.

35:18.t: Ben-oni means "son of my sorrow"; Benjamin means "son of the right hand".

35:21.t: Eder: the KJV spells it Edar.

36:2.t: and following: Oholibamah and Basemath; the KJV spells them Aholibamah and Bashemath.

36:24.t: "Mules": as in the KJV. The Hebrew word is rare and may mean hot springs.

36:37.t: "The River": probably the Euphrates. Shaul: the KJV spells it Saul.

37:3.t: "Robe of many colors": the KJV's "coat of many colours". The Hebrew may mean a long robe with sleeves.

37:28.t: "Pieces of silver": the unit is not named, probably shekels (about 230 grams of silver).

37:35.t: "Grave": the Hebrew is Sheol, the place of the dead.

"Grave" (Hebrew Sheol): the place of the dead, pictured as deep under the earth, where good and bad alike go. The KJV renders it "grave", "hell" or "pit". In the Old Testament it does not by itself mean a place of punishment. The Greek equivalent is Hades.

38:2.t: Shua: the KJV spells it Shuah.

38:14.t: "The entrance to Enaim": the KJV's "an open place" and "openly", where the Hebrew names a place, Enaim.

38:21.t: "The entrance to Enaim": the KJV's "an open place" and "openly", where the Hebrew names a place, Enaim.
"Shrine prostitute": the Hebrew word here differs from the ordinary word for prostitute in verse 15.

38:18.t: "Seal and its cord": the KJV's "signet, and thy bracelets".

38:29.t: Perez means "breaking out"; Zerah may mean "brightness". The KJV spells them Pharez and Zarah.

40:1.t: "Cupbearer": the KJV's "butler", the servant who served the king's wine.

40:16.t: "Baskets of white bread": the KJV's "white baskets"; the Hebrew may mean either.

41:2.t: "Among the reeds": the KJV's "in a meadow".

41:45.t: Zaphenath-paneah and Potiphera: the KJV spells them Zaphnath-paaneah and Poti-pherah. On is Heliopolis.

41:51.t: Manasseh sounds like "forget"; 41:52 Ephraim sounds like "fruitful".

42:9.t: "Where the land is unprotected": the KJV's "the nakedness of the land".

42:12.t: "Where the land is unprotected": the KJV's "the nakedness of the land".

42:27.t: "Stopped for the night": the KJV's "the inn", meaning a camping place.

43:21.t: "Stopped for the night": the KJV's "the inn", meaning a camping place.

44:5.t: "Divination": seeking hidden knowledge by signs, here by means of a cup.

44:15.t: "Divination": seeking hidden knowledge by signs, here by means of a cup.

45:6.t: "Plowing": the KJV's "earing", an old word for plowing.

45:22.t: "Pieces of silver": the unit is not named; if shekels, about 3.5 kilograms of silver.

46:4.t: "Close your eyes": the KJV's "put his hand upon thine eyes", that is, be with you at your death.

46:9.t: Pallu, Puvah, Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Bela: the KJV spells them Phallu, Phuvah, Jimnah, Ishuah, Isui, Belah.

47:31.t: "At the head of his bed": as in the KJV. The Greek Old Testament reads "on the top of his staff", which Hebrews 11:21 follows.

48:14.t: "Crossing his arms": the KJV's "guiding his hands wittingly", meaning on purpose.

48:16.t: "The Angel": capitalized as in the KJV.

48:22.t: "One portion": the Hebrew word is shekem, which may also point to the town of Shechem.

49:6.t: "Lamed oxen": the KJV's "digged down a wall". The Hebrew can mean either; most modern Bibles read "hamstrung oxen".

49:10.t: "Until Shiloh comes": as in the KJV. The Hebrew may also mean "until he comes to whom it belongs"; Christian readers have long taken it of the Messiah.

49:12.t: "Darker than wine ... whiter than milk": the KJV reads "red with wine ... white with milk"; the Hebrew allows both.

49:19.t: Gad sounds like the Hebrew for "raiders" and "attack".

49:24.t: "By the name of the Shepherd": the KJV's "from thence is the shepherd". Shepherd and Stone are titles of God.

50:24.t: "Come to your aid": the KJV's "visit you".

1:1.t: "God" (Hebrew Elohim): the word is plural in form, but used with singular verbs when it means the God of Israel, so it is translated "God". The same word can mean "gods" when it refers to the gods of other nations (31:30, "my gods").

1:2.t: "Spirit" (Hebrew ruach): the word means spirit, wind and breath. "The Spirit of God was hovering" follows the KJV. Some read "a mighty wind", but the verb "hovering" (used of a bird over its young in Deuteronomy 32:11) fits a living presence better.

2:4.t: "The LORD" (Hebrew YHWH): God's personal name, probably pronounced Yahweh and explained in Exodus 3:14 as "I AM". Jewish readers stopped saying it aloud and said Adonai, "Lord", instead, and the KJV followed that custom by printing LORD in capitals. We do the same.

15:6.t: "Counted it to him as righteousness" (Hebrew tsedaqah, "righteousness"; hashab, "count, credit"): righteousness here means being right with God, and "counted" is a bookkeeping word, to credit to an account. Paul quotes this verse as the foundation of justification by faith (Romans 4:3, Galatians 3:6); James uses it to show that real faith acts (James 2:23).

22:2.t: "Whom you love" (Hebrew ahav): the first use of the word "love" in the Bible is a father's love for his son, in the same verse that asks him to give that son up. ahav covers love of every kind, between family members, friends, spouses, and between God and His people.

24:27.t: "Steadfast love and faithfulness" (Hebrew hesed and emet): hesed is loyal, committed love that keeps its promises, especially within a covenant. No single English word covers it; the KJV uses "mercy", "kindness" and "lovingkindness". This translation uses "steadfast love" for God's hesed and "kindness" or "loyalty" for human hesed (as in 24:49). emet means firmness, reliability, truth. The pair "hesed and emet" appears often and describes God's character (Exodus 34:6).
